answer: Persistent Work Ledger requires each identity to sign a unique quill-marked transaction chain whose history is anchored to a physical mesa-based relay node. Cloning that chain forks the ledger, and honest nodes reject any branch lacking continuous co-signed receipts, so a sybil's copy stays hollow and unusable. Each fake identity must therefore rent distinct relay hardware and sustain real daily signing costs, making cloning more expensive than honest participation.
